items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-27
items.q: I'm reading a book right now about New Orleans. I mean, I got in this buddy Stahl wrote it.

ctx.x: Well, I was young for that. Believe me, I was young. That was when my daddy was playing out at Spanish Fort. In fact, we used to go out there. I used to go out there with him in the afternoon around one or two o'clock. And then my mother and my sister would catch the streetcar. Streetcar, there were no automobiles in those days. You'd catch, there was a train that used to start at Rampart and Canal. You'd go all the way up. I don't remember. Go out and go out West End Boulevard. You'd cut around and go right down…

coaches on the back. They'd have like an open air coach. And they'd have about two or three coaches on a streetcar. So if they'd have a big crowd, they'd be able to move them along. Because there was no two-way. There was no two-way. They had to go to the end of the line and come back and start over again. There was only one deal on that. I'm reading a book right now about New Orleans. I mean, I got in this buddy Stahl wrote it. It's very interesting. I'm reading right now about the epidemic of yellow fever when…
